title: Tapping Past Reserves for Land Reclamation Works
what_it_is: Tapping Past Reserves for Land Reclamation Works

sections.label: Funding flood and coastal infrastructure
sections.summary: Smaller infrastructure can be funded by Ministry budgets, major infrastructure may be borrowed for, and reclamation costs can be met from Past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Smaller scale infrastructure like localised flood barriers for public assets like hospitals and bus depots can be funded from the budgets of Ministries.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: For long-lived major infrastructure, such as sea walls, the Government will look at the option of borrowing to spread the cost across the generations which will benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Where the measures include land reclamation, the land reclamation costs can already be met from Past Reserves.

sections.label: Reclaimed land as Past Reserves
sections.summary: Reclaimed land is protected as Past Reserves, sale proceeds accrue to them, and using them for reclamation follows the Reserves Protection Framework.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The land created through reclamation will be protected as part of Past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: When such land is subsequently sold, the proceeds accrue fully to Past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The reclamation of land is in essence a conversion of Past Reserves from financial assets to state land.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: This use is not a draw on Past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The use of Past Reserves to fund reclamation costs is in accordance with the Reserves Protection Framework, which is agreed between the President and the Government.
